Time: 3 min. Teaching intent: Retrieve prior knowledge before revealing the method.
Talk track: What does a congested channel force you to change?
Expected answer / misconception: Placement, assignment, stackup, or technology; rerun the constraint check after the change.
Visual: The three conditions identify what must be compared.

Time: 4 min. Teaching intent: Teach the mechanism or design rule.
Talk track: Line width, spacing, layer count, and via rules bound how many nets can cross a channel. Trace the visual in order: route demand; available tracks; design-rule check. Connect this mechanism to the worked example: Synthetic check: if a channel needs 12 tracks but a chosen rule allows only 9, revise layer count or placement; do not waive the rule silently. Boundary: Track counts are synthetic teaching data.
Expected answer / misconception: Ask students to explain the link between adjacent elements; a conceptual diagram is not a measurement.
Visual: Native diagram encodes the causal or design relationship.
[Sources]
R2: IEEE EPS HIR 2024, Ch. 13: Co-Design | https://eps.ieee.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/HIR_2024_ch13_HIR_Co-Design.pdf
R3: IEEE EPS HIR 2024, Ch. 22: Interconnects | https://eps.ieee.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/HIR_2024_ch22_2D-3D.pdf

Time: 4 min. Teaching intent: Work the example step by step.
Talk track: Set up the case: Synthetic check: if a channel needs 12 tracks but a chosen rule allows only 9, revise layer count or placement; do not waive the rule silently. Identify the starting information, state the reasoning step aloud, then ask what observation would check the conclusion. Stop before the next slide's question is answered.
Expected answer / misconception: Students must identify the input, the inference, and the check. Track counts are synthetic teaching data.
Visual: Three-part reasoning path separates the example from its verification.

Time: 4 min. Teaching intent: Teach the mechanism or design rule.
Talk track: A dense bump field must reach legal routing channels; logical connectivity alone does not prove physical escape. Trace the visual in order: bump assignment; via escape; edge channel. Connect this mechanism to the worked example: Sketch inner-row bump escape for a chiplet. If two required routes cross on one layer, add a legal layer transition or change the bump assignment.
Expected answer / misconception: Ask students to explain the link between adjacent elements; a conceptual diagram is not a measurement.
Visual: Native diagram encodes the causal or design relationship.

Talk track: Can a perfect netlist still be unroutable?

Time: 4 min. Teaching intent: Teach the mechanism or design rule.
Talk track: Signals, power, and ground must be planned together because current loops and impedance depend on physical geometry. Trace the visual in order: power delivery; signal path; ground return. Connect this mechanism to the worked example: On the floorplan, draw a high-speed signal beside its reference return and then mark where the power path enters the compute die.
Expected answer / misconception: Ask students to explain the link between adjacent elements; a conceptual diagram is not a measurement.
Visual: Native diagram encodes the causal or design relationship.
